fact: An opinion piece by a named analyst says Mali's universal access fund is fed by a legal levy of 1% to 2% of operators' turnover, run by AGEFAU under the Prime Minister's office, and that the fund is collected today with chronic delays and operator arrears; no amount is given, and the date is the document's publication date.

The Prime Minister's office reports that AGEFAU's board adopted a revised 2026 budget of FCFA 27,886,688,000 for the universal access fund agency, against FCFA 41,151,471,000 initially, a fall of 32% inside the same budget year as projects are spread over 2026 and 2027; this is not a comparison of two budget years.

The Prime Minister's office reports that in the first half of 2026 AGEFAU collected FCFA 23,178,333,210 (56% of a FCFA 41,151,471,000 forecast) and spent FCFA 3,188,967,162 (8% of the annual budget); the fund's own collections and spending are both given.

The fund agency collected FCFA 23.18bn in the first half of 2026 and is financing network extension, access centres, school computer rooms and training of 1,000 young people from its revised 2026 budget.

On 22 July 2026 AGEFAU signed two four-year renewable conventions with the education and employment ministries, and its director general said the fund has invested over FCFA 17 billion in education since its creation, building and equipping universal access centres.

AGEFAU itself reports that its board adopted a revised 2026 budget of FCFA 27,886,688,000 against FCFA 41,151,471,000 initially, a fall of 32% within the same budget year, with projects spread over 2026 and 2027; this is not a comparison of two budget years.
The fund agency's revised 2026 budget pays for network extension in 162 localities, 80 universal access centres, 100 Wi-Fi huts, school computer rooms and training of 1,000 young people.

Le Pays reports the AGEFAU director general saying the fund spent nearly FCFA 3.7 billion in 2018-2024 and projects of over FCFA 13.5 billion since 2025, over FCFA 17 billion in all, on school and training-centre access centres, Wi-Fi huts and equipment.
Budget tables: the budget for 2026 gives 24,314,962,000 XOF to 103 digital line(s). Dated by the budget document.
Budget tables: the 7 digital line(s) held in both years total 10,339,800,000 XOF for 2026 against 9,935,715,000 for 2025, +4.1 per cent; 103 lines are held for 2026. Dated by the budget document.
